words.notes: v3.5 Lesson 6. Palm back: pages-layout/numbers.htm "Anyway, as a general rule do 1-5 palm back." o/one.htm shows the sign only as an image.
words.face_note: Numbers stay neutral (no expression invented)
words.quote: (Since the number "1" uses an index finger handshape and not a "D" handshape).

words.notes: v3.5 Lesson 6.
words.face_note: Numbers stay neutral (no expression invented)
words.quote: The sign for "two" (2) in ASL is done with the index finger and middle finger. When signed in isolation it is (generally) done palm back.

words.notes: v3.5 Lesson 6.
words.face_note: Numbers stay neutral (no expression invented)
words.quote: The sign for "three" or "3" in ASL is done with the thumb, index finger, and middle finger. When signed in isolation it is (generally) done palm back.

words.movement: hands move apart, beyond the width of the body
words.notes: v3.5 Lesson 6. The size turn is not in the exam (SMALL was dropped).
words.face_note: Lifeprint describes no face or head marker for this sign
words.quote: Another sign for "big" is made by forming "flat hands" with both of your hands in front of you, palms facing inward. Move your hands beyond the width of your body - the further the distance, the larger the word described.

words.handshape: right index; left open palm up
words.movement: flick the 'coin' toward the person being paid (directional)
words.notes: v3.5 Lesson 6. Reserve word: replaces SMALL (s/small.htm gives palms facing and the movement but no handshape). TEACH-ONLY: directional.
words.face_note: Lifeprint describes no face or head marker for this sign
words.quote: Think of having a coin in the palm of your left hand. You place the tip of your right index finger on the coin, then flick the coin to the person whom you are paying.

words.notes: v3.5 Lesson 6. No repeat is described, so one meeting.
words.face_note: Lifeprint describes no face or head marker for this sign
words.quote: The sign for "more" uses flattened "O" hands. Bring both "O" hands together.

words.movement: twist both hands quickly, palms in to palms (somewhat) forward
words.notes: v3.5 Lesson 6. One twist (Lifeprint: a single twist seems more final). Scored with the existing 'turn' detector, both hands.
words.face_note: The basic FINISH sign mentions no expression
words.quote: Each hand should face you, with your fingers pointing upward. ... Twist both hands quickly

words.location: out in front, about belly height
words.movement: each hand moves in a small circle (forward, out, back, in)
words.notes: v3.5 Lesson 6. Reserve word: replaces TEA (t/tea.htm gives only the handshapes; the movement is shown only in the animation). NAME (first reserve) was skipped: n/name.htm gives no contact point. TEACH-ONLY.
words.face_note: Lifeprint describes no face or head marker for this sign
words.quote: Both hands are in a relaxed flat hand shape.. ... palms facing up ... Out in front of you, about belly height. ... Each hand moves in a small circle.

words.handshape: flattened O on the open base hand
words.notes: v3.5 Lesson 6. TEACH-ONLY: scored with the 'tap' detector it collided with BREAD in the teacher self-test (BREAD recognised as MONEY).
words.face_note: Lifeprint describes no face or head marker for this sign
words.quote: The sign for money uses a flattened "O" (as if holding onto some money) and smacks it (lightly) twice onto the palm of the base hand.

words.handshape: palm-up O opening to a loose 5
words.notes: v3.5 Lesson 6. TEACH-ONLY (handshape change during the lift).
words.face_note: h/how-much.htm: "You should furrow your eyebrows a bit when asking such questions."
words.quote: a good variation to use is the one-handed version that moves upward while changing a palm-up "O" into a loose-5 handshape.
